dedupe_keys.name: international and sectoral variation in industrial energy prices 12 sectors in 48 countries 1995 2015

description: This dataset gives sector-level energy prices for 12 industrial sectors in 48 countries from 1995 to 2015. The Harvard Dataverse record says prices are weighted averages of fuel-specific prices by fuel consumption, in two measures, the Variable Weights Energy Price Level (VEPL) and the Fixed Weights Energy Price Index (FEPI), built mainly from International Energy Agency data with a documented method to reduce missing points; it also gives usage guidelines and a ready-made instrumental variable. It was deposited by M. Sato in February 2019 and is at version 3.1 (November 2019, a small update to some tax-inclusive FEPI variables), with one downloadable data table of about 3.3 MB, a PDF codebook and Stata scripts, free under CC0. Coverage is 48 countries. Caveats: the series ends in 2015, the method is documented in the related Energy Economics paper, and the author's affiliation is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives industrial energy cost inputs to test how price shocks and carbon pricing change sector competitiveness and production in economic impact models. Related catalogue records include the Iran industrial utility prices and the EIA Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey.
